result.strongest_objection: The doc's load-bearing evidence was measured on the wrong artifact, so its central claims fail premise verification as written. The mutation table's conclusion ('The prototype kills all 16 bound mutants, plus S1-S3, W1 and TM1', V8), the §3/AC-3 claim that 'the whole host/daemon package passes plain and under -race on the prototype' (V10: 279.8s plain, 521.3s race, count=200 finish race run), and AC-3's 'All are green (prototype: V10)' were all executed against the pre-rename r1 prototype. The r2 revision renamed the seam field to finishNow and rewrote its doc comment — i.e., the exact diff this doc specifies and the executor will commit — but the doc's own log (§4 header, V17) admits the post-rename tree was only re-verified for vet, a 50-count race subset of the finish tests, and mutants S1-S3 and W1. For the specified artifact, 17 of the 20 AC-2 mutant-kill attributions (P1-P6, Q1-Q6, R1-R6, TM1) and the full package plain/race batteries are asserted by transitivity from a different source tree, not verified. The rename is almost certainly behavior-neutral, but this doc sets its own standard that every factual claim carries a V-row, and the claims that carry the row's safety case currently do not, for the diff actually being proposed. The doc applies this same honesty rule to itself for AC-4 ('I did not run the full ./... or verify_ail.sh') but not for the r1-to-r2 delta.
result.catch: V8's 16-mutant table, the TM1 load-bearing-pin kill, and V10's package battery all predate the finishNow rename; only S1-S3 and W1 were re-run post-rename (V17). Alternatively, if the mechanical-rename argument is accepted, explicitly re-label §4's 'Prototype killer' column and V10's header as r1-prototype evidence and add to AC-2/AC-3 a sentence mirroring AC-4's disclosure: that the executor's run is the first verification of the r2 diff.

Also change §3's sentence to 'The whole host/daemon package passes plain and under -race on the post-rename prototype (V18)', change §4's trailing claim to 'The r2 prototype kills all 20 mutants (V18; the pre-rename prototype did the same, V8)', and have AC-3 cite V18 instead of V10. If the re-run cannot be done before submission, the minimum acceptable revision is to annotate §4 header ('P/Q/R/TM1 kill attributions verified on the pre-rename prototype; the r2 diff's first verification is AC-2 at execution time') and §3/AC-3 ('package green verified on the pre-rename prototype; AC-3 at execution is the first package run of the r2 diff'), matching the disclosure standard the doc already applies to AC-4.

result.strongest_objection: The no-fallback clock change introduces a nil-function panic for daemons not initialized by New, but the claimed exhaustive construction audit is not established by V13/V14. Their searches miss populated value literals such as `d := Daemon{...}`, package-alias-qualified literals, and zero-value declarations such as `var d Daemon`. Thus §3's safety premise—that every daemon reaching the finish route receives finishNow—is still unverified.
result.catch: V14's `&Daemon\{|Daemon\{\}` pattern does not enumerate every Daemon construction, and V13 searches only `&Daemon{`. Passing existing tests does not establish that omitted construction paths cannot reach the handler.
result.proposed_fix: Replace the exhaustive-construction claim with a type-aware audit at the measurement commit: enumerate composite literals, new expressions, and zero-value declarations whose resolved type is host/daemon.Daemon, including package aliases. Add a verification-log row listing each construction and whether it can reach the finish handler. Initialize finishNow explicitly at every reachable construction or route construction through New; retain the no-silent-fallback behavior. Until that audit is complete, describe V13/V14 as textual-search results rather than proof that all constructions are covered.

result.strongest_objection: In §4, mutant rows Q4 and Q6 state that T3 arm `approve-1` kills the `:271` upper bound (`> now+3600`), which relies on evaluating the record clock backwards in time (`T-1`) relative to the scope's `T+3600` expiry rather than setting a scope expiry above `now+3600`, though mathematically equivalent (`(T+3600) > (T-1)+3600`).
result.catch: Ensure the `finishNow` field comment in `host/daemon/daemon.go` explicitly warns both that it is not shared with `coordinator.Config.Now` and that tests may only mutate it before or between synchronous handler invocations.
result.proposed_fix: No changes required; the r2 verification entries (V14-V17) thoroughly resolve the conflict surface, struct-literal risk, and coverage vs. mutation-sensitivity premises.
